_about: PRO rewrite pass 8: era-2 scenes 118-150 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Vacation
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants a real vacation this offseason: two weeks, an island, no phones. You want to train. The brochure has been on the kitchen counter for a month, open to the same page.

choices.label: Go, and leave the ball home
choices.result: Two weeks on the island, no ball, no film, no phone. It's the best fortnight of the year, and you come back rested and in love all over again.

choices.label: Stay and train
choices.result: Training, alone, while {love_interest} goes with friends and sends pictures of the water every day. You're stronger by July and a little lonelier.

choices.label: Find an island with a field
choices.result: A beach town with a high school field, found after two hours of searching. Mornings for kicking, afternoons for the beach. Everyone wins, sort of.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: The Payday
scenarios.text: This is the contract that could set up your family for life, if you earn it this season. Your agent has a number in mind, and so does the club, and they're far apart.

choices.label: Make the season undeniable
choices.result: Every practice counts, every rep, every film session. Nothing about this season will be an accident, and you're exhausted and proud by December.

choices.label: Let your agent do the talking
choices.result: Every contract conversation goes to your agent, and you keep your head on kicking. It works, mostly, though you check your phone after every practice.

choices.label: Talk it through at home
choices.result: A long evening at home, talking it through. Their calm becomes your calm, and you sleep better for the rest of the season.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Discount
scenarios.text: The club offers less than the market and asks you to take it because 'you're family here'. The general manager says it twice, and puts his hand on your shoulder the second time.

choices.label: Take the discount
choices.result: The discount, accepted. The club remembers it, and so does the locker room, and you never quite know if it was generous or foolish.

choices.label: Meet in the middle
choices.result: The middle ground, found by your agent over two weeks of calls. Everyone is a little unhappy and fine, which your agent says is how you know it's fair.

choices.label: Test the market next spring
choices.result: Next spring's open market, it is. You kick like it all year, and every practice feels like an audition for twenty-nine other clubs.

scenarios.title: The Holdout Talk
scenarios.text: Your agent slides the club's offer across a restaurant table: less than a kicker in your division got last spring, with a pay cut in year two. 'We hold out,' your agent says. 'You stay home from camp until they pay you what you're worth.'

choices.label: Sign it and say why
choices.result: You sign, then tell your agent you'd rather kick for a fair number than sit at home waiting for a better one. Your agent calls it leaving money on the table. {coach} calls it the best news of the week.

choices.label: Hold out
choices.result: You stay home when camp opens. The club fines you every day, talk radio calls you greedy, and two weeks later you sign for a little more and walk into a locker room that moved on without you.

choices.label: Call the general manager yourself
choices.result: You call the general manager directly, which agents hate. You get a better guarantee in year two and an agent who sulks for a month.

choices.label: Ask for the honest read
choices.result: The agent you hired for honesty admits the offer is fair for a kicker and a holdout would cost more than it gains. You sign, and you don't regret it.
choices.lock_text: having hired an agent who tells you the truth

scenarios.title: First Day of School
scenarios.text: Your kid's first day of school falls on a Thursday practice day. The backpack has been packed since Sunday, and there's a photo planned by the front door at seven-thirty.

choices.label: Ask to come in late
choices.result: An hour's grace from {coach}, granted without a pause. You're there for the photo, the backpack, and the wave at the classroom door.

choices.label: Go to practice and watch the video
choices.result: Practice, and a video from home at lunch. You watch it four times in the locker room, and {holder} watches it with you.

choices.label: Plan the whole morning
choices.result: The morning, planned to the minute with {coach} and the family: drop-off at seven-forty, meeting at eight-fifteen. You make both, barely.

scenarios.title: The Snapper Retires
scenarios.text: The long snapper you've trusted for years is done: his back, his age, his wife's patience. He asks you, of all people, to speak at his farewell dinner.

choices.label: Speak from the heart
choices.result: What it's like to trust someone without ever looking back: you tell the room. He cries first, and then everyone else does.

choices.label: Keep it light and true
choices.result: Three funny stories and one true one. The room loves it, and he asks for a copy of the speech to show his kids.

choices.label: Say a few words
choices.result: A few short words and a raised glass of water. He hugs you anyway, hard, and says it was perfect, and his wife writes you a note.

scenarios.title: The Podcast
scenarios.text: A popular podcast wants you for a full hour. The host is famous for getting athletes to say too much, and three of your teammates have already regretted going on.

choices.label: Prepare and stay disciplined
choices.result: Prepared, disciplined, and still funny. It's a good episode with no headlines, and the host admits you were a hard interview.

choices.label: Be yourself on air
choices.result: Funny and honest for an hour, until one joke about a teammate gets clipped everywhere. You apologize to him before he hears it.

choices.label: Turn the podcast down
choices.result: No, politely. The host says something snide about kickers on the next episode, and your teammates send it to you, delighted.

scenarios.title: The National Deal
scenarios.text: A national brand wants you for a commercial that would air during every game this year: you, a ball, and a talking dog. The shoot is during your bye week.

choices.label: Sign on for the commercial
choices.result: Signed. You're on every broadcast all season, the talking dog becomes famous, and the shoot eats your entire bye week, which you never get back.

choices.label: Shoot it in the offseason
choices.result: The offseason, or nothing, you tell them politely. They agree, the dog waits, and your bye week stays your own, with your family.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: No commercial this year. You'd rather be known for kicking than for the dog, and a punter gets the part instead and loves it.

scenarios.title: A New City, Mid-Career
scenarios.text: A new club, a new town, and a locker room that has already decided whether you're a mercenary. The last kicker was popular, and his photo is still on the wall.

choices.label: Win the room
choices.result: Every name learned, every team meal attended, every question asked. By midseason the room is yours, and the old photo comes down.

choices.label: Let the work talk
choices.result: Few words and a great many kicks. The room comes around by October, slowly and completely, and nobody mentions the old photo again.

choices.label: Help the young specialists
choices.result: The young specialists get your help from day one: rides, film, advice. They become your biggest supporters, and the room follows their lead.

scenarios.title: The Public Relationship
scenarios.text: Your relationship becomes a topic of public interest after a photo goes around, and {love_interest} didn't sign up for that. There are strangers in the comments of their private account.

choices.label: Protect {love_interest}
choices.result: Nothing about home, posted ever again, not even a photo of the dog. {love_interest} notices, and is quietly grateful, and the strangers lose interest by spring.

choices.label: Set boundaries together
choices.result: What stays private and what doesn't: decided together, at the kitchen table, with a list. It feels like a team, which it is.

choices.label: Let it blow over
choices.result: It'll blow over, you decide. It takes much longer than you thought, and {love_interest} deletes the account without telling you.

scenarios.title: The Family Conversation
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} start talking about starting a family, late at night, and neither of you knows the right time. The schedule, the contract, the next city: everything feels uncertain.

choices.label: Decide on now
choices.result: Now, you both say, at almost the same moment. It's terrifying and right, and you laugh for ten minutes afterward.

choices.label: Plan around the seasons
choices.result: A plan, built around the contract and the seasons: when, where, who helps. It's sensible, and it makes the dream feel real.

choices.label: Agree to wait
choices.result: Waiting, for now, you both agree. The conversation comes back every few months, a little more urgent each time, and a little warmer.

scenarios.title: The Sponsored Posts
scenarios.text: A supplement-free sports drink company offers to pay you for sponsored posts. The product is fine, mostly, and the contract has a clause about 'authentic enthusiasm'.

choices.label: Take the deal
choices.result: The deal, signed. The posts do well, the money is real, and the 'authentic enthusiasm' feels a little hollow every time.

choices.label: Test it for a month
choices.result: A month of actually drinking it before you post a word. It's genuinely good, and your posts say so honestly.

choices.label: Keep your page yours
choices.result: No sponsored posts, ever. Your page stays yours, full of your dog, your family and very bad photos of sunsets.

scenarios.title: The Long-Term Commitment
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants to talk about where you'll live after football. It's a quiet Sunday, and they've made a list of places on the back of an envelope.

choices.label: Let {love_interest} choose
choices.result: Their choice, from the envelope: a town near the coast, near their family. It's the right call, and you both know it.

choices.label: Make the list together
choices.result: A list together, with pros and cons in two colors. Your hometown wins by a point, and {parent} cries on the phone when you tell him.

choices.label: Say there's still time
choices.result: There's still time, you say. {love_interest} says there isn't always, and puts the envelope away in a drawer you both pretend not to see.

scenarios.title: The Pregnancy
scenarios.text: {love_interest} is pregnant, and the due date falls right in the middle of the season. You're thrilled, terrified, and already counting weeks on the team schedule.

choices.label: Plan to be there
choices.result: You tell {coach} now that you'll miss a game if the baby comes on a Sunday. The coach says it's the right call and means it.

choices.label: Make a plan with everyone
choices.result: You make a plan with {love_interest}, the coach and both families: who's on call, which flights, which bags. It feels like a playbook, and it helps.

choices.label: Hope for the bye week
choices.result: You hope the baby comes in the bye week. You also keep a bag packed in the car and check your phone at every break.

scenarios.title: The Baby's First Year
scenarios.text: Sleepless nights with a newborn, in the middle of the season. The baby wakes at two and four, practice starts at eight, and you've started falling asleep in film sessions.

choices.label: Take the night shifts
choices.result: The night shifts on your off days, every one. You're tired and closer to {love_interest} and the baby than you've ever been to anyone.

choices.label: Sleep in shifts by schedule
choices.result: A sleep schedule, written on the fridge like a practice plan. It works, roughly, and nobody falls asleep in a meeting again.

choices.label: Ask the grandparents for help
choices.result: The grandparents, invited for a month. Everyone sleeps, the house is loud and full, and {parent} becomes a diaper expert.

scenarios.title: The Daycare
scenarios.text: Finding daycare in a city where you might not live next year. Every good place has a waiting list, and every waiting list asks how long you'll be in town.

choices.label: Visit every place
choices.result: Six daycares, visited in one week, with a notebook. You pick the best one and get on the list by being honest about the contract.

choices.label: Ask the team families
choices.result: The other team families, asked at the next game. They have a list, a group chat and a spot opening up in March.

choices.label: Hire a nanny for the season
choices.result: A nanny for the season, and a decision later. It's expensive and easy, and the baby adores her within a week.

scenarios.title: The In-Laws
scenarios.text: {love_interest}'s family visits for two weeks during the season: parents, a grandmother, and a brother-in-law who is certain that kicking is easy and has a lot of advice about it.

choices.label: Be the perfect host
choices.result: Every evening at home with them: dinners, card games, the grandmother's long stories. {love_interest} notices, and so does the grandmother.

choices.label: Keep your routine
choices.result: Your routine, unchanged, and you see them at dinner every night. It's polite and a little distant, and {love_interest} doesn't say anything.

choices.label: Plan their days
choices.result: Their days, planned by you: the museum, the stadium tour, a lake. Everyone has something to do, and the brother-in-law gets a practice pass.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Video Series
scenarios.text: You start a video series teaching kids how to kick, filmed in your backyard on a phone. The first episode has more views than your team's highlight reel.

choices.label: Make it really good
choices.result: Real drills, real mistakes, real fixes, and a lot of editing late at night. Coaches start using it in practice.

choices.label: Bring {holder} in
choices.result: {holder}, invited for an episode on holding. It's the most popular one by far, because {holder} is much funnier on camera than you.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: One video a month on your phone, unedited. It's honest and charming, and it never takes more than an hour.

scenarios.title: The Wedding Planning
scenarios.text: Wedding planning in the middle of the season, and every decision is a phone call: flowers between meetings, the menu on the team bus, seating charts at midnight.

choices.label: Take every call
choices.result: Every call, even in the minutes between meetings. {love_interest} feels it, and the seating chart is perfect, and you're exhausted.

choices.label: Hire a planner
choices.result: A planner, hired, and the big decisions saved for Mondays. It works beautifully, and it costs more than the cake and the flowers combined.

choices.label: Leave it to {love_interest}
choices.result: Most of it, left to {love_interest} until the offseason. They manage it all, and they remember exactly who didn't help.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Net in the Living Room
scenarios.text: You set up a kicking net in the living room for winter practice, right in front of the television. {love_interest} has opinions, mostly about the lamp that's already broken.

choices.label: Move it to the garage
choices.result: The net, moved to the garage, with a space heater. Peace returns to the house, the lamp is replaced, and the garage becomes your favorite room.

choices.label: Negotiate a deal
choices.result: A deal: weekdays only, and you hang the paintings that have been leaning on the wall since you moved in. Everyone wins.

choices.label: Keep the net
choices.result: The net stays where it is. Some arguments are worth having, you decide, and you kick very carefully around the brand-new lamp all winter.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Parade
scenarios.text: Your hometown throws you a parade after your best season: a fire truck, the high school band, and {parent} in the front car, waving like he's the one who kicked.

choices.label: Ride with {parent}
choices.result: The front car, beside {parent}, waving until your arm hurts. He doesn't stop smiling for the entire route, and neither, in the end, do you.

choices.label: Give a speech at the end
choices.result: A short speech on the courthouse steps, thanking the town. The high school team cheers loudest, and the kicker asks for your gloves.

choices.label: Ride the route and slip away
choices.result: The route, a few waves, and then a quiet exit to {parent}'s porch. The town understands; the band plays on without you.

scenarios.title: A Teammate Holds Out
scenarios.text: Your closest teammate is holding out for a new contract and wants you to say something publicly. The front office is watching who stands with him.

choices.label: Back him publicly
choices.result: You back him publicly in front of the cameras. He's grateful for good, and the front office remembers your name in a different way.

choices.label: Back him privately
choices.result: Privately, at his kitchen table, you say you're with him all the way. He understands why it stays private, and wishes you'd said it louder.

choices.label: Speak for the room
choices.result: You tell reporters the whole team wants him back and leave the money to the people who handle it. Both sides nod, neither is thrilled.

scenarios.title: The Prime-Time Game
scenarios.text: Your first prime-time game in years, and the national broadcast crew wants an interview at the team hotel the night before. They want a 'human' story.

choices.label: Tell them a real story
choices.result: One good story, about kicking into a fence with {parent}. It runs before kickoff, and {parent} watches it on repeat.

choices.label: Give them ten minutes
choices.result: Ten polite minutes, then bed. The story they run is fine and forgettable, and you sleep well and wake up ready.

choices.label: Decline and watch film
choices.result: A polite no, and film in your room instead until midnight. The crew talks to the punter, who is absolutely delighted.

scenarios.title: The Career Milestone
scenarios.text: You reach a career milestone the club makes a big deal about: a graphic on the scoreboard, a ball in a case, and a question about how you want to celebrate.

choices.label: Celebrate with the specialists
choices.result: Dinner with the specialists, on you, at the steakhouse. {holder} gives a speech that is mostly about {holder}, and it's perfect.

choices.label: Celebrate at home
choices.result: The people who knew you before, at home: {parent}, {sibling}, old friends. The ball in the case goes on {parent}'s mantel.

choices.label: Thank the room one by one
choices.result: Every person in the building, thanked one by one: trainers, equipment staff, the snapper, the cafeteria. It takes all day and it's worth it.

scenarios.title: The Big Second Contract
scenarios.text: Your agent says this is the contract that matters, the one that sets the rest of your life, and the club agrees, eventually, after a month of silence.

choices.label: Hold firm for your number
choices.result: Three tense weeks of holding firm. You get your number, and lose some sleep getting it, and the general manager doesn't smile at you for a while.

choices.label: Take the fair deal early
choices.result: A fair deal, taken early, and you stop thinking about it entirely. Your agent calls it smart, and means it, and you sleep well all spring.

choices.label: Decide it at home
choices.result: The decision, made at home, at the kitchen table. The number matters less than you thought, and you sign happily.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Charity Game
scenarios.text: You organize a charity game in your hometown with players from five clubs: a high school field, a sold-out crowd of four thousand, and a lot of favors called in.

choices.label: Run every detail yourself
choices.result: Every detail, run by you: buses, jerseys, the national anthem singer. It's exhausting, and it raises far more than anyone expected.

choices.label: Put {best_friend} in charge
choices.result: {best_friend} runs the whole day, with a clipboard and a whistle. It's the most fun either of you has had in years.

choices.label: Hire an organizer
choices.result: An event organizer who actually knows what they're doing. It runs perfectly, and it feels a little less like yours on the day.

scenarios.title: The Captaincy
scenarios.text: The team votes for captains, and for the first time in the club's history a kicker is on the ballot. Your name is written on the whiteboard in the locker room, misspelled.

choices.label: Ask for the vote
choices.result: Why a kicker can lead too: you tell the room in two minutes, plainly. You win by four votes, and they fix the spelling on the whiteboard.

choices.label: Let the room decide
choices.result: No campaign at all. The room votes you in anyway, by more, and that means more than any speech would have.

choices.label: Take your name off the ballot
choices.result: Your name, erased from the whiteboard by you. A linebacker who wanted it more gets the patch, and thanks you privately.

scenarios.title: The Kid Who Copies Your Routine
scenarios.text: A high school kicker's video goes around the internet: he copies your whole routine, down to the last step and the way you tug your sleeve.

choices.label: Send him a message and cleats
choices.result: A message and a pair of cleats. His video of opening the box gets more views than yours ever did.

choices.label: Show him one fix
choices.result: A short reply video showing him one thing to fix. Kickers everywhere try it, and his school's coach writes to thank you.

choices.label: Smile and show {love_interest}
choices.result: A smile, and the video shown to {love_interest} over dinner, twice. You don't reply, and you think about it all week.

scenarios.title: The Coordinator's Son
scenarios.text: The new special teams coordinator's son is a kicker on the practice squad. He's polite, talented, and his father watches every one of his kicks with great interest.

choices.label: Out-kick him every day
choices.result: Better than him every single day of camp. It's awkward and undeniable, and the coordinator starts watching your kicks just as closely.

choices.label: Help the kid
choices.result: His plant foot, fixed with your help. The coordinator watches and says nothing, and something between you changes for good.

choices.label: Ask the coordinator directly
choices.result: How exactly is the job decided? You ask him straight, in his office. He respects the question and gives you a fair, specific answer.

scenarios.title: The Endorsement Renewal
scenarios.text: Your biggest sponsor wants to renew, with new conditions: more appearances, more posts, more of you. The contract is twice as long as the first one.

choices.label: Accept the conditions
choices.result: Accepted. The money is good, and your weeks get much shorter, and you start to recognize the sponsor's photographer at your house.

choices.label: Halve the appearances
choices.result: The appearances, negotiated down by half, line by line. They agree, grudgingly, and you keep your Tuesdays and your sanity.

choices.label: Walk away from the renewal
choices.result: The renewal, politely declined. You get your Tuesdays back, and your agent finds a smaller, kinder deal within a month.

scenarios.title: The Rival Club Calls
scenarios.text: A rival club's general manager catches you at an awards dinner and makes it very clear, without saying it outright, that they'd pay you a lot more the next time you're free.

choices.label: Keep it between you and your agent
choices.result: Your agent hears every word, and nobody else does. You kick the rest of the season like a player with options, calmly and well.

choices.label: Tell your own club
choices.result: Your own general manager hears about the conversation from you, the next morning. They appreciate it more than they say, and they remember it at contract time.

choices.label: Forget the conversation
choices.result: Forgotten, on purpose, by the time you're home. You kick the season out without thinking about it, and whatever comes in spring, comes.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Coach
scenarios.text: {holder} retires and joins the coaching staff, with a whistle and a new office. Now {holder} is your boss, and the first meeting is tomorrow.

choices.label: Keep the friendship
choices.result: The friendship stays, and you let {holder} coach you anyway. It works, mostly, and only gets strange at parties and team dinners.

choices.label: Set new rules together
choices.result: New rules, agreed over coffee: coach at the facility, friends on the weekend. It works better than either of you expected.

choices.label: Earn their trust fresh
choices.result: {holder}, treated like any new coach, and you earn their trust again from scratch. It's strange, and it makes you both better.

scenarios.title: The Motivation Slump
scenarios.text: Nothing's wrong. That's the problem: practice feels like a job, the job feels like nothing, and you haven't been nervous before a game in a month.

choices.label: Take a real break
choices.result: Days off, taken seriously for once: no film, no phone, a long hike in the hills. Some of the spark comes back, slowly, by the end of the month.

choices.label: Talk to someone
choices.result: Out loud, for the first time, to the team psychologist. It's uncomfortable and it helps, and you go back the next week.

choices.label: Set a secret goal
choices.result: A goal nobody else knows about, written on a card in your wallet. Practice has a point again, and you catch yourself smiling during warmups.
